chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated, saying: Abu Sa'id narrated to me from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
He was asked about a man who made a bequest for a hajj, but his executor assigned it to a person.
He said: "His executor must bear its cost and place it in a hajj just as he directed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
"Then whoever changes it after hearing it, its sin is only upon those who change it."

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a will or bequest
key_terms.بَدَّلَهُ: changed or altered it from its intended form
key_terms.حَجَّةٍ: a bequest for a hajj to be performed
key_terms.وَصِيُّهُ: his executor, the one responsible for carrying out the will
key_terms.يَغْرَمُهَا: he must compensate for it from his own liability
key_terms.يُبَدِّلُونَهُ: those who alter or substitute it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an executor changes a deceased person's bequest for hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a bequest for hajj must be carried out exactly as instructed by the deceased. If the executor alters that bequest, he is liable for the loss and bears the sin of changing the will, in accordance with the Qur'anic principle regarding altering a valid testament.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2923 - Ibn Muskan narrated, who said that Abu Sa'id reported from Abu Abdullah (as):
He was asked about a man who instructed in his will for a Hajj to be performed on his behalf, but his executor used the funds for another purpose.
Imam (as) said: "The executor must bear the cost himself and ensure that it is used for a Hajj as specified in the will. For Allah (swt), the Exalted, says:
'But if anyone changes it after hearing it, the sin shall be upon those who make the change.' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:181)."
